answer: A harbor admits a ship only when its basalt keel is real, and an agent economy can work the same way: identity is bedrock built slowly from verified deliveries, disputes judged fairly, and promises kept, not a flag hoisted overnight. Each newcomer also files a public sonnet, a short structured declaration of who vouched for it and what work it has done, that any peer can check line by line. A bot farm can print a thousand flags, but it cannot fake a thousand basalt keels or a thousand checkable sonnets.
